title: Cook's second voyage in the Resolution, 1772–75
summary: Cook went south to find the great southern continent or prove it a myth, crossing the Antarctic Circle three times and reaching 71°10′S, then looped through the tropical Pacific. A Raʻiatean, Mai, went to London in the Adventure; a man of Bora Bora, Hitihiti, sailed in the Resolution.

events.label: The Antarctic Circle crossed
events.source: Wikipedia, Second voyage of James Cook
events.text: At 66°36′S 39°35′E, the first recorded crossing of the Antarctic Circle. The Resolution crossed it twice more.

events.label: Hitihiti of Bora Bora joins the Resolution
events.text: A man of Bora Bora came aboard at Raʻiatea, taking the place of another passenger, Porea. The Wellcome Collection dates his time aboard 17 September 1773 to 4 June 1774; he sailed with the ship to Tonga, New Zealand, the Antarctic and Easter Island before going home.
events.doubt: The end of his stay is given in some sources as 22 April 1774, when Cook brought him back to Tahiti, and in the Wellcome Collection as 4 June.

events.label: Farthest south, 71°10′S
events.source: Wikipedia, Second voyage of James Cook
events.text: Cook turned back in the ice at 71°10′S, 106°54′W. Hitihiti, a man of Bora Bora, was aboard.
events.doubt: Wikipedia's account gives both 30 January and 3 February 1774 for this day.

events.label: Grass Cove: ten of the Adventure's men killed
events.text: Tobias Furneaux sent a cutter with ten armed men ashore to collect wild greens. They did not return. The next day Lieutenant James Burney found the remains of ten men on the beach at Wharehunga Bay. New Zealand's history sites hold that they were killed by Ngāti Kuia and Rangitāne, led by the Ngāti Kuia chief Kahura.
events.doubt: The accounts differ over who led the party: Rowe, a master's mate, in one, a midshipman, Woodhouse, with eight hands in another.
